title: Halvorsen Institute
text: The Halvorsen Institute is a research organisation headquartered in Brindlemark. It was founded in 1921 to study glaciology.

title: Brindlemark
text: Brindlemark is a port city on the Ostrel River, known for its clock tower and its annual lantern festival.

title: Ostrel River
text: The Ostrel River rises in the Kesh Mountains and flows 410 kilometres to the Amber Sea.

title: The Salt Cartographer
text: The Salt Cartographer is a 1911 novel by Ilse Moravec about a mapmaker who charts an inland salt desert.

title: Ilse Moravec
text: Ilse Moravec was a Tarnovian novelist and essayist who was born in 1874 and died in 1950.

title: Tarnovia
text: Tarnovia is a mountainous republic whose literature flourished in the early twentieth century.

title: Lantern Ash
text: Lantern Ash is an opera composed by Davit Karelian that premiered in 1958 at the Grand Hall.

title: Davit Karelian
text: Davit Karelian was a composer who was born in the Republic of Sorrel and later taught in Marlow.

title: Republic of Sorrel
text: The Republic of Sorrel is a small coastal nation whose capital is Velmora.

title: Marlow
text: Marlow is a university town famous for its rowing regatta and its botanical garden.

title: Kesh Mountains
text: The Kesh Mountains form a range with peaks above four thousand metres and heavy winter snowfall.

title: Amber Sea
text: The Amber Sea is a shallow inland sea with low salinity and abundant fisheries.

title: Glaciology
text: Glaciology is the scientific study of glaciers, ice sheets and other natural ice formations.

title: Clock towers
text: A clock tower is a tall structure with one or more clock faces, often built in a town square.

title: Opera
text: Opera is a form of theatre in which music has a leading role and the text is sung.

title: Grand Hall
text: The Grand Hall is a concert venue with excellent acoustics and seating for two thousand people.

title: Novel
text: A novel is a long work of narrative fiction, normally written in prose and published as a book.

title: Cartography
text: Cartography is the study and practice of making maps of land, sea and sky.

title: Salt desert
text: A salt desert is an arid region where evaporation has left thick crusts of salt on the ground.

title: Lantern festival
text: A lantern festival is a celebration in which people release or display illuminated paper lanterns.

title: Coastal nations
text: Coastal nations often develop their capitals around natural harbours and trading ports.

title: Rowing regatta
text: A rowing regatta is a series of boat races held over a fixed course on a river or lake.

title: Composer
text: A composer is a person who writes music, including songs, symphonies and operas.

title: Essayist
text: An essayist is a writer who produces essays, short nonfiction pieces on a particular subject.

title: Botanical garden
text: A botanical garden is a collection of documented living plants kept for research and education.
